problem_motivation.content: The oxidation behavior of ultrafine-grain AlCoCrFeNi HEA under specific processing conditions and its resulting microstructural evolution are the focus of investigation, implying a need to understand how ultrafine grains affect oxidation.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: This work investigates the effect of ultrafine-grain microstructure on the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA).

problem_motivation.content: There is a need for advanced materials with superior surface oxidation resistance and improved mechanical properties at high temperatures to extend the life of gas turbine components.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Thus, there is a need to develop advanced materials with superior surface oxidation resistance and improved mechanical properties at high temperature.

problem_motivation.content: Existing superalloys can only achieve modest increases in operating temperatures, and improved cooling consumes too much energy.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Improvements in superalloy technology can achieve only relatively modest increases in operating temperatures while the use of improved active component cooling could consume so much energy that the expected gain in engine performance would be significantly reduced.

prior_approach.content: Surface deformation techniques such as surface mechanical attrition treatment, shot peening, microwave processing, ultrasonic treatment, and UNSM have been used to refine microstructures and study their effect on oxidation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Surface deformation techniques including surface mechanical attrition treatment, [15] shot peening, [16] microwave processing, [17] and ultrasonic treatment [18] have been utilized to obtain fine-grain microstructure, and subsequently its effect on oxidation behavior was investigated. Similarly, ultrasonic nanocrystal surface modification (UNSM)-assisted thermal oxidation behavior of Ti 6 Al 4 V alloy was investigated.

prior_limitation.content: Unprocessed samples exhibit the formation of spinel oxides, which suggests a limitation in their oxidation resistance or oxide scale stability compared to processed samples.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: In addition, spinel Co(Cr,Fe) 2 O 4 /Fe(Co,Cr) 2 O 4 formation is also detected in the unprocessed oxidized samples.

prior_limitation.content: Prior studies on microstructural refinement and oxidation have only focused on conventional structural materials, leaving a gap for high entropy alloys.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: It is worth mentioning that all the prior studies on microstructural refinement and the oxidation behavior of the resulting materials were limited to conventional structural materials only. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, there has been no study on achieving remarkable oxidation resistance in HEAs through microstructural refinement.

causal_claim.content: The presence of grain boundaries in processed samples causes internal oxidation leading to Al-rich inner oxides.

causal_claim.content: Higher rotational speed leads to deeper depth of refinement (DOR) due to a thicker plastically deformed zone.

causal_claim.content: High temperature at higher rotational speed causes deeper DOR by favoring material flow through thermal softening.
causal_claim.evidence_span: High temperature at higher rotational speed favors the material flow through thermal softening and leads to deeper DOR.

causal_claim.content: Higher tool rotational speed results in highly refined sub-micrometer grain structures with a significant fraction of nanograins.

causal_claim.content: The highly refined grain structure of the SFP_1800 sample is caused by high strain-rate deformation resulting in dynamic recrystallization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thus, the highly refined grain structure of SFP_1800 sample is attributed to high strain-rate deformation resulting in dynamic recrystallization.

causal_claim.content: The evolution of the FCC phase is likely caused by BCC/B2 phase transformation during high strain-rate processing.

questions.question: Does the suppression of spinel oxides in AlCoCrFeNi HEA at 850–1050 °C depend on surface free energy exceeding a specific threshold, or is it strictly a function of grain boundary density and Cr out-flux?
questions.rationale: The paper attributes the lack of spinel to both high surface free energy and enhanced Cr diffusion via GBs; distinguishing these is required to determine if process parameters should target surface energy (e.g., via specific surface treatments) or grain boundary engineering.
questions.decision_use: If surface energy is the dominant factor, process optimization must focus on increasing surface energy independently of grain size; if GB density is dominant, strain rate must be maximized.
answer_requirements: Compare oxidation products (spinel presence/absence) in samples with identical grain boundary density but varying surface energies (e.g., via different pre-treatments or alloying additions), and measure surface free energy.
evidence_spans: The likely reason for the lack of spinel species in the processed samples is the high surface free energy, which suppresses the formation of spinel oxides.

questions.decision_use: Knowing the critical speed threshold allows setting a minimum process parameter to guarantee the formation of a protective chromia layer and prevent failure due to spinel scales.
